passage_text: Researchers conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy of the novel antihypertensive agent, Hypotensol, in adults with stage 1 hypertension. A total of 120 participants were enrolled and randomly assigned to either the Hypotensol group (n=60) or the placebo group (n=60). Baseline systolic blood pressure (SBP) was measured after a 5-minute seated rest. Participants received either Hypotensol 10 mg once daily or matching placebo for 8 weeks. SBP readings were taken at baseline and at week 8. Table 1 summarizes the mean SBP values and changes for each group. The Hypotensol group showed a mean reduction of 12.3 mmHg, whereas the placebo group exhibited a mean reduction of 3.1 mmHg. The mean reduction was therefore 9.2 mmHg greater with Hypotensol than with placebo.
stem: Which group experienced the greater mean reduction in systolic blood pressure?
explanation: The Hypotensol group had a mean reduction of 12.3 mmHg versus 3.1 mmHg for placebo.
trap: Assuming the placebo group had no reduction when it actually did.

stem: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the passage and Table 1?

options.A: The mean SBP reduction was larger in the Hypotensol group than in the placebo group.
options.B: The placebo group's mean SBP fell by 3.1 mmHg.
options.C: The between-group difference in mean SBP reduction was 9.2 mmHg.
options.D: Every participant given Hypotensol had an SBP reduction of at least 12.3 mmHg.

explanation: Correct: D) The table gives group means only; 12.3 mmHg is an average, so individual reductions must vary and some may have been smaller. Why the others are wrong: A) 12.3 mmHg exceeds 3.1 mmHg. B) The table lists -3.1 mmHg for placebo. C) 12.3 - 3.1 = 9.2 mmHg, as the passage states.
trap: Reading a group mean as the result every individual achieved.

stem: Which conclusion is best justified by these data?

options.A: In adults with stage 1 hypertension like those enrolled, 8 weeks of Hypotensol 10 mg lowered mean SBP more than placebo did.
options.B: Hypotensol should replace all other antihypertensive drugs.
options.C: Hypotensol is ineffective at lowering SBP.
options.D: Hypotensol is superior to every other antihypertensive drug.

explanation: Correct: A) Mean SBP fell 12.3 mmHg with Hypotensol versus 3.1 mmHg with placebo in the studied population over 8 weeks. Why the others are wrong: B) No other drug was tested, so replacement is not addressed. C) A 12.3 mmHg mean fall exceeds the placebo fall. D) The trial had no active comparator, so superiority to other drugs cannot be claimed.
trap: Extending a two-arm result to claims about other drugs or other populations.
